title: Replace stamp duty on home purchases with a broad land tax
action: Phase out stamp duty on residential property purchases over several years and replace the revenue with a broad-based annual tax on the unimproved value of land. Let low-income owners defer the tax until the property is sold.
why: Stamp duty taxes people for moving. It discourages older owners from downsizing and workers from moving closer to better jobs, so homes and labour are used less productively. A land tax raises the same revenue without that penalty.

evidence.source: Australia's Future Tax System: Report to the Treasurer, Part One (Henry review)
evidence.quote: Ideally, there would be no role for any stamp duties, including conveyancing stamp duties, in a modern Australian tax system. Recognising the revenue needs of the States, the removal of stamp duty should be achieved through a switch to more efficient taxes, such as those levied on broad consumption or land bases.

evidence.source: Shifting the Dial: 5 Year Productivity Review
evidence.quote: State and Territory Governments should move from stamp duties on residential and commercial properties to a broad-based land tax on the unimproved value of land.

evidence.source: Shifting the Dial: 5 Year Productivity Review
evidence.quote: A shift to land-based taxes should include provision for low income households to defer property taxes and fund them from their estate at death or on the sale of the asset

evidence.source: NSW Productivity Commission White Paper 2021: Rebooting the economy
evidence.quote: Replace inefficient taxes with more efficient ones. Start by replacing property transfer duty with a broad-based property tax on unimproved land values.

precedents.what: Phasing out conveyance duty in favour of general rates over 20 years from 2012.
Replacing stamp duty on commercial and industrial property with an annual property tax from 2024.

progress.what: Only the ACT has begun a full switch. New South Wales let first-home buyers choose an annual property tax instead of duty from January 2023, but closed the choice to new buyers in July 2023.

tradeoffs: Owners who recently paid stamp duty should not pay land tax as well (a transition, such as switching each property on its next sale, avoids this). Land tax revenue is steadier than stamp duty, but the switch costs revenue in the early years, which states may need to borrow against.
